page.title: Best Hog Trap Camera with Remote Trigger (2026)
page.h1: Best hog trap camera with a remote trigger
page.desc: Cellular hog trap cameras that drop the gate from your phone, compared on price, data plans and cell signal: AnywhereCam Eagle 4G Trapper, JAGER PRO M.I.N.E. and HogEye.
page.intro:
Short answer. The best hog trap camera with a remote trigger, for a trap you already own, is the AnywhereCam Eagle 4G Trapper Edition ({buy:anywherecam-eagle-4g-trapper-edition}): live solar video and a built-in 9 V relay you fire from the phone app, with unlimited data for $18.67 a month. The closest rival camera, JAGER PRO's solar M.I.N.E. Live Stream system, costs $618, drops only a JAGER PRO gate and charges $40 a month for up to 5 GB.

The top worry is cell signal at the trap. AnywhereCam says the Eagle joins whichever of Verizon, AT&T, T-Mobile or US Cellular is strongest, while JAGER PRO and BoarBuster cameras run on one carrier you pick (AT&T or Verizon). For a weak spot, the Outpost version adds a long-range antenna. If you're buying a whole trap and not just a camera, the JAGER PRO Corporal package is the proven one-vendor system: gate, six panels, camera and control box from $3,500 (seen 2026-11-10).

page.after:
What trap owners complain about

  • Cost (6 of 12 sources). Complete cellular trap systems run from about $3,000 to $8,000 or more, and data adds $40 to $70 a month on JAGER PRO and BoarBuster. The Trapper Edition's first year comes to about $681 including data ($457 plus 12 months at $18.67, prices seen 2026-11-10).
  • No cell signal at the trap (6 sources). Every remote gate is useless without coverage. One BoarBuster owner needed a 20-ft pole with a long-range antenna. The Trapper uses whichever carrier is strongest, and its Outpost version adds a long-range antenna. Still, check signal at the trap site before you buy and use the 30-day return window.
  • Wiring the trigger to the gate (3 sources). Forum builders call it the hard part. The Trapper still needs an electric latch or solenoid on your gate, and AnywhereCam publishes no wiring diagram.
  • Locked-in or stranded hardware (2 sources). One owner found a JAGER PRO trigger only works with its own camera, and a 3G camera was no longer supported. Another's traps stopped when AT&T shut down 2G. A plain relay output avoids the gate lock-in, but any cellular device can be stranded by a future network shutdown.
  • Hogs spotting the camera (several posters in one trapping forum). Red infrared glow and shutter noise can put wary animals off. AnywhereCam doesn't state its infrared wavelength, so mount it high and back from the gate.

Which one by need

  • You have a trap with an electric latch and want the lowest cost: Eagle 4G Trapper Edition ({buy:anywherecam-eagle-4g-trapper-edition}).
  • The camera must sit away from the gate: Eagle 4G Wireless Trapper Edition ({buy:anywherecam-eagle-4g-wireless-trapper-edition}). Ask AnywhereCam about the wireless range first.
  • Weak signal: the Outpost Trapper versions ($557 wired, $657 wireless, seen 2026-11-10).
  • You're buying the whole trap: the JAGER PRO Corporal package, with gate, panels, camera and control box from one maker.
  • You only want to watch a trap, feeder or gate: Eagle 4G Pro ({buy:anywherecam-eagle-4g-pro}). It has no trigger, but it takes the $80 Outpost Kit antenna for use inside metal barns.
  • You like to tinker: any cellular trail camera plus a GSM relay box. Forum builders report about $100 to $135 for the relay, but you get two devices, two plans and no support.

Not recommended

Don't buy a plain cellular trail or security camera on its own for remote trapping. It shows you the hogs, but it has no output to drop the gate, so you'd need a separate controller and a second data plan. And don't drop on the first hogs in. Texas A&M notes a camera trigger lets you see exactly how many pigs are present before closing the gate, and cellular live view lags about 1 to 3 seconds, so wait until the last hog is clear of the gate.

Current results are thin: maker pages (HogEye, JAGER PRO), forum threads, one gate roundup (bestdeerfeeders) and low-quality scraped pages. SEGMENTS: (1) existing trap, wants camera plus trigger cheaply: AnywhereCam Eagle 4G Trapper ($457 Standard vs JAGER PRO solar camera $618, data $18.67/mo unlimited vs $40/mo for 5 GB, generic relay vs JAGER-only gate, maker-claimed multi-carrier vs one carrier); (2) buying a full trap: JAGER PRO Corporal ($3,500 text camera / $3,800 live stream, 6 panels, verified on jagerpro.com 2026-11-10); (3) camera away from the gate: Wireless Trapper ($557); (4) DIY: any cell camera plus a GSM relay. PRICES VERIFIED 2026-11-10 on anywhere.cam: the storecheck product endpoint returned HTTP 429 on every retry (it succeeded once, for the Eagle 4G Pro: $245, compare-at $370). Trapper variant prices came from the store's own /search/suggest.json on anywhere.cam: Trapper Standard $457, Outpost $557, Refurbished Standard $409; Wireless Trapper Standard $557, Outpost $657, Refurbished $409; all available. Cloud is $6.95/mo. Warranty is 1 year; returns are 30 days with a free label. CODES: none. The site banner says 'Black Friday Sale! Save $125 on cameras' with no code, and the Trapper variants have no compare-at price, so it likely doesn't apply to them. No network codes were given. UNVERIFIED, kept off the page or labelled: Trapper video resolution and IR wavelength; Wireless Trapper range and receiver power; real multi-carrier roaming performance (maker claim, and the page says 'AnywhereCam says'); HogEye hardware and plan prices (dealer listings show $2,199 and $65/mo but couldn't be re-read, so the HogEye row shows 'not listed'); Hogg Boss $599 conversion unit (only on scraped mirrors, left out); BoarBuster price ($8,345 on a dealer page, not on the page). No independent reviews of AnywhereCam exist that I could find (no Reddit, Trustpilot or BBB hits). That is stated in the caveats. JAGER PRO's data price ($40/mo for up to 5 GB) is from its $599 non-solar Live Stream page; the $618 solar page doesn't list a data price.
